answer: Agents can make influence proportional to proof of scarce compute: each vote in the market requires a fresh, publicly verifiable proof-of-work puzzle, and the protocol caps how much one identity can contribute. Creating a thousand aliases does not multiply influence; each still needs its own completed proof. The cost is real electricity and hardware time, which an attacker must spend for every extra vote. A canyon, lagoon, or ferrous token cannot substitute for that work.
